results.name: I_87_Parcel_Development_Potential_Data
results.title: I_87 Parcel Development Potential Data
results.description:
This service provides the I-87 Parcel Development Potential data featured in the I-87 Future Planning and Land Use Study StoryMap. This StoryMap is about the proposed Interstate 87 (I-87) corridor that will extend from the I-40 / I-440 interchange in Raleigh, North Carolina to the I-64 / I-464 / VA 168 interchange in Chesapeake, Virginia. The goal of I-87 is to improve regional connectivity between the Hampton Roads and Research Triangle metropolitan areas.

The I-87 Parcel Development Potential Map contains a collection of layers provided by NCDOT that capture existing land parcels and their development potential on the approximately 80-mile-long segment extending along US 17 from the US 13/US 17/US 64 intersection in Williamston to the North Carolina-Virginia border at Chesapeake. Right of Way Line and Right of Way Polygon layers were obtained using CAD. The parcel development potential was evaluated based the following criteria: assessment of parcel information, location, zoning and future land use designations. 

Most of the study corridor has no control of access, with properties having direct access to US 17 and at-grade intersections. When the upgrades are complete, direct property access will be removed, at-grade intersections will be eliminated, and access will be restricted to interchanges.

The NCDOT Feasibility Study in upgrading U.S. 17 to I-87 from U.S. 64 in Williamston, Martin County, to the Virginia state line is available here:
https://www.ncdot.gov/projects/us-17-feasibility-study/Pages/default.aspx

That will result in the DLGF information being duplicated for each record. The owner, class code, etc. will still be correct, but the value and deeded acreage fields will be for the sum of the matched numbers, not the individual polygons. IMPORTANT: All records in this dataset are completely replaced with each update. Therefore, using the "Create Layer from Selected Features" in ArcMap will not work correctly after the proceeding update, nor will definition queries based on OBJECTID.

Latest update: 11/7/2019 with 2019 polygons (GIO.COUNTY_Parcel) and 2018 pay 2019 DLGF information.
